headline: A tech site has spotted an unreleased setting in Google's Gemini desktop app that suggests the AI could work across a whole computer without asking permission at every step.
score_reason: Pool score 4 lowered by 1: the headline reads like a confirmed plan, but this is an unreleased setting seen by one site, with no date from Google.
importance_line: Desktop users could one day hand Gemini longer tasks across their computer with fewer prompts, but this is an unreleased setting seen by one outlet, Google has given no date, and testing features sometimes stay unreleased for months.
summary: TestingCatalog reports that it found an 'Additional sandbox options' setting in the computer-use area of Google's Gemini desktop app, which suggests Gemini could work outside chosen folders, use the internet and other apps without asking approval at each step; a sandbox is the limited area an AI is allowed to work in. Purchases and legal sign-offs would still need a person's confirmation, and Google has not announced the feature or a release date.
notes: Single-outlet report on an unreleased feature; TestingCatalog itself says no launch timeline can be drawn from it.
